Work done by Guddu in 1 day = a/12

Ratio of work done by Rani, Priya and C:

questions.question: A container is normally filled in 5 hours. However, it takes 6 hours when there is a leak at the bottom. If the container is full, in what time would the leak empty it, if no water is allowed into the container during that period?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Time taken to fill the container normally = 5hr

Time taken to fill when leakage is present = 6hr

**Calculation**

Extra time taken to fill due to leakage = 6 - 5= 1hr

Let the volume of the tank to be V

Part of tank filled in 1hr at normal condition = V/5

Part of tank filled in 1hr in leakage condition = V/6

Part of tank leaked in 1hr = V/5 - V/6 = V/30

So the tank leak 1/30 volume in 1hr

**∴ He full tank is leaked within 30hr.**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. Due to leakage in the bottom it is filled in 20 hours. If the tank is full, and the pipe is closed, how much time will the leak take to empty the entire tank?
questions.solution:

Time taken by pipe to fill the tank = 15 hours

Due to leakage, the time taken to fill the tank = 20 hours

**Concept Used:**

Rate of Leakage = Initial filling rate – Filling rate with leakage

**Calculation:**

⇒ Initial rate of filling the tank = (1)/(Time)=(1)/(15)

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank with leakage = 20 hours

⇒ So, Filling rate with leakage = (1)/(20)

⇒ Therefore, Rate of leakage = (1)/(15)-(1)/(20)=(4-3)/(60)=(1)/(60)

questions.question: Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours. If both taps are opened together, then how much time (in hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tap A can fill the tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours.

**Concept Used:**

If a pipe can fill or empty a tank in x hours then in 1 hour it can fill or empty 1/x part of the tank

**Calculation:**

Let, the total tank is 1 part

Tap A can fill the tank in 6 hours

That means in 6 hours tap A can fill 1 part of the tank

⇒ In 1 hour tap A can fill 1/6 part of the tank

Tap B can empty the tank in 10 hours

That means in 10 hours tap B can empty 1 part of the tank

⇒ In 1 hour tap B can empty 1/10 part of the tank

In 1 hour part of the tank will be filled when both taps are opened together is (1/6 – 1/10)

⇒ (5 - 3)/30

⇒ 2/30

⇒ 1/15

To fill the tank time taken is 1/(1/15) hours

⇒ 15 hours

**∴ If both taps are opened together the tank will be filled in 15 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Tap A can fill the tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours

LCM of 6 and 10 is 30

Let, the tank be of 30 units

In 1 hour tap A can fill (30/6) = 5 unit of the tank

In 1 hour tap B can empty (30/10) = 3 unit of the tank

When both the taps are opened together in 1 hour tank will be fill (5 - 3) = 2 unit

**∴ To fill the tank total time needs (30/2) = 15 hours**

questions.question: R can finish a work in 6 days if he works 10 hours a day. S can finish it in 5 days if he works 8 hours a day. If both start a work and work daily for 6 hours, the work will be finished in _____ days.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R can finish a work in 6 days if he works 10 hours a day.

S can finish it in 5 days if he works 8 hours a day.

Both start a work and work daily for 6 hours.

**Formula used:**

Work done per hour by R = Total work / (Number of days × Hours per day)

Work done per hour by S = Total work / (Number of days × Hours per day)

Total work done per hour by R and S = Work done per hour by R + Work done per hour by S

Total days to complete the work = Total work / (Total work done per hour by R and S × Hours per day)

**Calculations:**

Work done per hour by R = 1 / (6 × 10)

⇒ Work done per hour by R = 1 / 60

Work done per hour by S = 1 / (5 × 8)

⇒ Work done per hour by S = 1 / 40

Total work done per hour by R and S = (1 / 60) + (1 / 40)

⇒ Total work done per hour by R and S = (2 + 3) / 120

⇒ Total work done per hour by R and S = 5 / 120

⇒ Total work done per hour by R and S = 1 / 24

Total days to complete the work = 1 / (1 / 24 × 6)

⇒ Total days to complete the work = 24 / 6

⇒ Total days to complete the work = 4

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 36 and 45 minutes, respectively, whereas pipe C alone can fill the tank in 15 minutes. B and C are opened together for 15 minutes, and then both are turned off and A is opened. Pipe A will empty the tank in (in minutes):
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken to empty a full tank by Pipe A = 36 min

Time taken to empty a full tank by Pipe B = 45 min

Time taken to fill the tank by Pipe C = 15 min

B and C opened together = 15 min

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 36, 45 and 15 is 180

Efficiency of A = 180/36 = 5 units/min

Efficiency of B = 180/45 = 4 units/min

Efficiency of C = 180/15 = 12 units/min

Efficiency of B and C together = (12 – 4) = 8 units/min

B and C opened for 15 min = (8 × 15) units

⇒ 120 units

Now,

Pipe A will empty the tank = (120/5) mins

⇒ 24 mins

**∴ Required time is 24 mins**

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 20 days. B and C together can complete the same work in 15 days. If A, B and C all work together, then the same work gets completed in 10 days. How many days will A and C together take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete a work in 20 days.

B and C together can complete the same work in 15 days.

A, B and C all work together, then the same work gets completed in 10 days.

**Concept Used:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(20, 15, 10) = 60 units

Efficiency of A and B together = 60/20 = 3 .......(i)

Efficiency of B and C together = 60/15 = 4 ........(ii)

Efficiency of A, B and C together = 60/10 = 6. .......(iii)

Solve (i) and (iii)

Efficiency of C = 6 - 3 = 3

Put in (ii)

Efficiency of B = 4 - 3 = 1

Put in (i)

Efficiency of A = 3 - 1 = 2

Efficiency of A + C = 3 + 2 = 5

A and B together can complete a work = 60/5 = 12 days

**A and C together take to 12 days complete the same work.**

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern separately in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. A waste pipe can drain off 40 litres per minute. If all the three pipes are opened, the cistern fills in one hour. The capacity (in litres of the cistern) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two pipes can fill a cistern separately in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively.

A waste pipe can drain off 40 litres per minute.

If all three pipes are opened, the cistern fills in one hour.

**Formula used:**

Let the capacity of the cistern be x litres.

Rate of filling by the first pipe = x / 36 litres/minute

Rate of filling by the second pipe = x / 45 litres/minute

Rate of emptying by the waste pipe = 40 litres/minute

Net rate of filling when all three pipes are open = (x / 36) + (x / 45) - 40 litres/min
